Salvē! Salvēte!

hello (to one person; to several)

The everyday greeting of Plautus and Terence (Lewis & Short: “very freq. and class.”).

Other words

  • Salvus sīs! Salva sīs! — hello, be well (to a man; to a woman)

    also used · classical · Traupman 17; Plaut. Mil. 902: Salvē, architecte. — Salva sīs.

    Often the reply to salvē.

  • Avē! Avēte! — hail! good day

    also used · classical · Cael. in Cic. Fam. 8.16.4; Mart. 3.95.1 (Lewis & Short s.v. aveō)

    More formal than salvē: in Martial the morning greeting, and the Avē of the Vulgate (Luc. 1.28). Lewis & Short doubts that Cicero used it.

Examples

  • Salvē. — Salvē. — Quid agis?

    Hello. — Hello. — How are you?Plaut. Men. 138

  • Ō Syre noster, salvē: quid fit? quid agitur? — Rēctē. — Optimē est.

    Hello, Syrus my friend: how’s it going? how are things? — Fine. — Splendid.Ter. Ad. 883–884

  • ut lībertī servīque māne salvēre, vesperī valēre sibi singulī dīcerent

    that each of his freedmen and slaves should say hello to him in the morning and goodbye in the eveningSuet. Galb. 4 (Lewis & Short s.v. aveō)

  • Salvē et tū.

    Hello to you too.Traupman 15, 18

  • Salvē, adulēscēns. — Et tū multum salvētō, adulēscentula.

    Hello, young man. — And a very good day to you, young lady.Plaut. Rud. 2.4.3 (Lewis & Short s.v. salveō)

See also how are you?, say hello to … for me, goodbye, hey!, I’m glad you’re back, bless you.
